record.what_it_does: Pumble is a team chat and collaboration app (Slack-like messaging platform) that exposes a REST API and MCP server for sending messages, managing channels, reactions, files, and users in a workspace.
record.auth_notes: For full third-party apps, Pumble uses an OAuth2 authorization-code flow (consent screen at app.pumble.com/access-request, token exchange at api-ga.pumble.com/oauth2/access) that issues non-expiring user and bot access tokens. For simpler personal/single-user use, the 'API' addon lets a user generate a static API key that is passed as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. The MCP server (mcp.pumble.com/mcp) is authenticated with a 'token' header (user/bot token) plus an 'x-app-token' (app key), both obtained by creating and installing a Pumble app/addon.
record.access_notes: Any workspace admin/user can install the free 'API' addon and self-generate an API key immediately, or create a custom app from scratch (Configure apps > Create app) to get OAuth2 client credentials and MCP tokens, all within Pumble's free-forever plan — no paid tier or vendor approval step is documented for obtaining working credentials.
